chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who prays the prayer alone, then he finds a congregation, he said: He should pray with them and make it the obligatory prayer.
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they pray alone and then join a congregation for the same prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'Taqabbul al-Fard' (acceptance of the obligatory prayer) when joining a congregation after praying alone, preventing unnecessary repetition. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the social and communal value of Salāt al-Jamāʿah, where the individual's prior prayer is validated rather than voided. This prevents the burden of double prayer while encouraging participation in the collective worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the man who prays the Salāt alone, then he finds a Jam’at. Heasws said: ‘He should pray Salāt with them, and he should make it to be an Oblligatory (Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Salah (prayer) alone then finds a congregation.
He (the Imam) said, ’He can perform Salah (prayer) with them and make it to be an obligatory one.”’
